arxiv-1803-04085.title: Temporal processing and context dependency in C. elegans mechanosensation
arxiv-1803-04085.creator: Mochi Liu, Anuj K Sharma, Joshua W Shaevitz, Andrew M Leifer
arxiv-1803-04085.description: Abstract A quantitative understanding of how sensory signals are transformed into motor outputs places useful constraints on brain function and helps reveal the brain’s underlying computations. We investigate how the nematode C. elegans responds to time-varying mechanosensory signals using a high-throughput optogenetic assay and automated behavior quantification.

arxiv-1810-00382.description: Abstract The Hlawka Zeta Function is a Dirichlet series defined geometrically which provides an integral representation of the number of lattice points contained in the dilation t ​ D tD for some star shaped region D ⊂ ℝ 2 D\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} and some real number t ∈ ℝ + t\in\mathbb{R}^{+} .

arxiv-2303-15049.title: InterviewBot: Real-Time End-to-End Dialogue System to Interview Students for College Admission
arxiv-2303-15049.creator: Zihao Wang, Nathan Keyes, Terry Crawford, Jinho D. Choi
arxiv-2303-15049.description: Abstract We present the InterviewBot that dynamically integrates conversation history and customized topics into a coherent embedding space to conduct 10 mins hybrid-domain (open and closed) conversations with foreign students applying to U.S. colleges for assessing their academic and cultural readiness.

arxiv-2308-00404.title: Challenging the Myth of Graph Collaborative Filtering: a Reasoned and Reproducibility-driven Analysis Conference: Seventeenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems; September 18–22, 2023; Singapore, Singapore Seventeenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys ’23), September 18–22, 2023, Sing
arxiv-2308-00404.creator: Vito Walter Anelli, Daniele Malitesta, Claudio Pomo, Alejandro Bellogín, Eugenio Di Sciascio, Tommaso Di Noia
arxiv-2308-00404.description: Abstract . The success of graph neural network-based models (GNNs) has significantly advanced recommender systems by effectively modeling users and items as a bipartite, undirected graph. However, many original graph-based works often adopt results from baseline papers without verifying their validity for the specific configuration under analysis. Our work addresses this issue by focusing on the replicability of results.

arxiv-2308-09890.title: Inductive-bias Learning : Generating Code Models with Large Language Model
arxiv-2308-09890.creator: Toma Tanaka, Naofumi Emoto, Tsukasa Yumibayashi
arxiv-2308-09890.description: Abstract Large Language Models(LLMs) have been attracting attention due to a ability called in-context learning(ICL). ICL, without updating the parameters of a LLM, it is possible to achieve highly accurate inference based on rules “in the context” by merely inputting a training data into the prompt.

arxiv-2312-17346.title: STanHop : Sparse Tandem Hopfield Model for Memory-Enhanced Time Series Prediction
arxiv-2312-17346.creator: Dennis Wu † Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu ∗† Weijian Li ∗† Bo-Yu Chen ‡ Han Liu †♮ † Department of Computer Science, Northwestern University, Evanston, IL 60208 USA ‡ Department of Physics, National Taiwan University, Taipei 10617, Taiwan ♮ Department of Statistics and Data Science, Northwestern University, Ev
arxiv-2312-17346.description: Abstract We present STanHop-Net ( S parse Tan dem Hop field Net work) for multivariate time series prediction with memory-enhanced capabilities. At the heart of our approach is STanHop , a novel Hopfield-based neural network block, which sparsely learns and stores both temporal and cross-series representations in a data-dependent fashion.

arxiv-2506-03984.title: Around the World in 24 Hours Probing LLM Knowledge of Time and Place
arxiv-2506-03984.creator: Carolin Holtermann, Paul Röttger, Anne Lauscher
arxiv-2506-03984.description: Abstract Reasoning over time and space is essential for understanding our world. However, the abilities of language models in this area are largely unexplored as previous work has tested their abilities for logical reasoning in terms of time and space in isolation or only in simple or artificial environments.

arxiv-2507-07884.title: Conspiracy to Commit: Information Pollution, Artificial Intelligence, and Real-World Hate Crime
arxiv-2507-07884.creator: Alberto Aziani, Michael V. Lo Giudice, Ali Shadman Yazdi
arxiv-2507-07884.description: Abstract Is demand for conspiracy theories online linked to real-world hate crimes? By analyzing online search trends for 36 racially- and politically-charged conspiracy theories in Michigan (2015–2019), we employ a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to predict hate crime occurrences offline.

pmc-10741517.title: The Impact of BRAF Mutation Status on Survival Outcomes and Treatment Patterns among Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients in Alberta, Canada
pmc-10741517.creator: R Liam Sutherland, Devon J Boyne, Darren R Brenner, Winson Y Cheung, David Wong
pmc-10741517.description: Simple SummaryColorectal cancer can present in diverse ways due to genetic and molecular variations. This study focused on metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) and its correlation with a specific genetic mutation known as v-raf murine sarcoma viral oncogene homolog B1 (BRAF). Among the 488 mCRC patients studied, 42 (11.4%) were found to have the BRAF mutation.

pmc-12128804.title: CENTRAL SENSITIZATION IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN
pmc-12128804.creator: Snežana Tomašević-Todorović, Tijana Spasojević
pmc-12128804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SUMMARYCentral sensitization is the mechanism of nociplastic pain and leads to an overemphasized response to a painful stimulus (hyperalgesia) or pain to stimuli that do not otherwise cause pain (allodynia). Persistent nociceptive pain is a risk factor for nociplastic pain, which can often occur in isolation or combination with other types of pain, most often in patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain (osteoarthritis, lumbar and cervical syndrome, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, complex regional pain syndrome, tendinopathy, etc.).

pmc-12437494.title: Psycho-social profile of patients with chronic neuropathic pain and spinal cord stimulation outcome: preliminary finding from an Italian sample recruited at the University Hospital of Verona (Italy)
pmc-12437494.creator: C Perlini
pmc-12437494.description: IntroductionSpinal cord stimulation (SCS) is used to treat chronic neuropathic pain (CNP) resistant to other therapies and procedures. The treatment involves implanting a device that delivers electrical stimulation along the ascending nerve pathways. According to the bio-psycho-social model of pain, the success of SCS is influenced by more than just the technical aspects of the procedure.

pmc-12581926.title: Survey Questions on Quantity and Frequency Are Differentially Effective by Age in Predicting Future Alcohol Consumption
pmc-12581926.creator: Sarah Callinan, Simon D'Aquino, Ben Riordan, Jonas Raninen, Michael Livingston, Paul M Dietze, Gerhard Gmel, Robin Room
pmc-12581926.description: IntroductionCross sectional research has demonstrated that screening tool questions on frequency of alcohol consumption are a better predictor of dependence and harmful drinking in younger adults; questions about quantity per occasion are a better predictor in older adults. The aim of this study is to see if this relationship also holds longitudinally.

pmc-12641303.title: Association of adult caregiver depression with developmental disorder likelihood in Ugandan children perinatally exposed and unexposed to HIV
pmc-12641303.creator: Jorem Emmillian Awadu, Bruno J Giordani, Alla Sikorskii, Sarah Zalwango, Catherine Abbo, Amara Ezeamama, Anonymous, María Teresa Muñoz Quezada, Patricia Kipkemoi, Primrose Nyamayaro, Dixon Chibanda, Itziar Familiar, María Teresa Muñoz Quezada, Patricia Kipkemoi, Primrose Nyamayaro, Dixon Chibanda
pmc-12641303.description: We assessed whether higher caregiver depression is associated with increased likelihood of caregivers rating their children as screening positive for developmental disorders—autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, emotional behavioral disorder, and functional impairment (FI)—among Ugandan children perinatally exposed and unexposed to HIV. Children and their primary caregivers were followed for 12 months.

pmc-13603494.description: Scan-assisted interocclusal registration may vary with record extent and occlusal support.
